# D5 — Synthesis

One-bullet recommendation per concern. Each cites the dimension(s) the
decision rests on. Sources in [`../citations.md`](../citations.md).

## PVC model — one StatefulSet per operator

- **One StatefulSet per operator** with `volumeClaimTemplates` for the
  single PVC; do not use one StatefulSet with N replicas because scale-
  down semantics couple the per-tenant lifecycle to the highest ordinal.
  See [D1](pvc-statefulset-vs-deployment.md). At N=1, a Deployment+PVC
  is functionally equivalent and slightly simpler; the StatefulSet's
  `volumeClaimTemplates` is preferred only because it auto-provisions and
  binds the PVC by name without separate manifest plumbing [1][2].
- Leave `persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy` at the default
  (`whenDeleted: Retain, whenScaled: Retain`) [2]. With Longhorn's default
  StorageClass at `Delete` reclaim, deleting the PVC erases the data —
  retain at the controller level so accidental controller deletion does
  not cascade [3][4].

## PodSecurity profile + fsGroup approach — restricted + fsGroup + OnRootMismatch

- **Keep PodSecurity `restricted` on tenant namespaces.** For a sandbox
  running untrusted code, the baseline profile is below the security
  threshold (allows `seccomp: Unconfined`, no `runAsNonRoot` requirement)
  [5]. See [D2](pvc-permissions-non-root.md).
- **Pattern:** `securityContext.fsGroup: <per-tenant-gid>`,
  `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`, `runAsNonRoot: true`,
  `runAsUser: <uid>`. No init container [6][7][10][11]. Longhorn's CSI
  applies fsGroup for Filesystem-mode RWO PVCs with `fsType` set
  (`fsGroupPolicy: ReadWriteOnceWithFSType`) [9][10]. First mount does
  the recursive chown; subsequent mounts skip via OnRootMismatch.
- Use **Filesystem mode**, not Block mode. Block mode requires
  `supplementalGroups: [6]` to access the Longhorn block device under
  restricted, which is workable but adds an unusual group binding [10][14].

## Tailnet vs cluster-internal OTEL route — go cluster-internal

- **Call the in-cluster Collector Service directly** at
  `otel-collector.otel.svc.cluster.local:4317`. Do NOT route in-cluster
  Pod → in-cluster OTEL via the tailnet hostname.
  See [D3](tailscale-operator-egress.md). Evidence:
  - Operator-egress on k3s + Flannel-over-Tailscale collapses to 2-3
    Mbit/s due to MTU mismatch (issue #16820) [19].
  - Long-lived TCP/gRPC streams hang and time out on ProxyGroup replica
    restart; Tailscale has closed this as not-planned (issue #16162) [20].
  - The cluster-egress feature is explicitly "currently in beta" per
    Tailscale's docs [16].
  - The egress path is multi-hop (tenant Pod → ClusterIP → headless
    Service → proxy Pod → tailnet → ingress proxy → Collector) when the
    Collector is also exposed via `tailscale.com/expose` for external
    callers [16][17][18]. Direct in-cluster is one hop.
  - gRPC client-side `dns:///` resolver gotcha adds ~30s connect delay
    over Tailscale [21] — solvable with `passthrough:///` but
    additional fragility.
- The existing `otel-collector.<tailnet>.ts.net:4317` exposure remains
  correct for **external** Claude wrappers. Two routes for two audiences.

## NetworkPolicy pattern — namespaceSelector + podSelector + DNS allowance

- **Use Pattern B** (`namespaceSelector` on `kubernetes.io/metadata.name:
  otel` AND'd with `podSelector` on the Collector's Pod labels, in the
  same `to:` entry). See [D4](networkpolicy-otel-patterns.md). k3s
  enforces this via its embedded kube-router NPC [24][29].
  - `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` is auto-injected and immutable [23] —
    stable selector without any operator action.
  - AND-combining `namespaceSelector` and `podSelector` in one entry
    narrows reach to Collector Pods only, not the whole otel namespace
    [22].
  - CNI-portable (works the same on Flannel+kube-router as on Calico or
    Cilium, unlike ipBlock) [22][27].
- **Avoid Pattern A** (`ipBlock` on Collector ClusterIP). ClusterIP is
  unstable across Helm reinstalls / cluster rebuilds, and ipBlock
  semantics for in-cluster IPs are explicitly undefined per the k8s spec
  [22] and explicitly broken on Cilium-class CNIs [27].
- **Add an explicit DNS allowance** to kube-system / k8s-app: kube-dns on
  UDP 53 AND TCP 53. The project's current default-deny excludes the
  Service CIDR (10/8), which silently breaks cluster-internal name
  resolution — masquerading as a Collector reachability problem. This
  is independent of the Collector-specific rule; both are mandatory.

## Cross-cutting recommendation: bring Tailscale CGNAT into the deny list

- The project's current NetPol does not exclude CGNAT (`100.64.0.0/10`)
  from egress. After adopting the in-cluster route for the Collector
  (above), there is no remaining reason for tenant Pods to reach CGNAT
  destinations directly. **Add `100.64.0.0/10` to the deny ranges** for
  symmetry with the RFC1918 exclusion. This closes the path where a
  compromised sandbox could exfiltrate to arbitrary tailnet nodes.
  This is not strictly a research finding — it is a synthesis derived
  from the asker's stated security posture and the choice in this
  document not to use the tailnet egress path.

## What this research does NOT settle (handoff to the brainstorm session)

- **Specific YAML / Helm values** — explicitly out of scope per the
  prompt; the brainstorm session designs the build.
- **PVC sizing and Longhorn replica/dataLocality settings** — operational
  parameters, not k8s plumbing.
- **Tenant identity / who-is-an-operator** — the controller-per-operator
  recommendation assumes the tenant model is "one human operator per
  Pod"; if that changes, revisit D1.
- **Backup strategy for tenant `$HOME`** — Longhorn snapshot/backup
  config is orthogonal to the controller choice and was noted as a
  consideration in [D1](pvc-statefulset-vs-deployment.md) but not
  designed here.
